items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: when I went to work with the Basie Band in '51... Clark Terry was playing the trumpet and Wardell Grey (PHONETIC) was playing the tenor saxophone

ctx.x: No, nobody writes for a clarinet. So if you don't write for it, you don't play it. But that was pretty well my favorite instrument. As a matter of fact, when I went to work with the Basie Band in '51, when I went -- that was January, 1951 -- I went to his band primarily as a clarinet player, because I was replacing Buddy De Franco, who was an excellent clarinet player, one of the best jazz clarinet players there ever was. So, in replacing him, Basie was kind enough to remember that I was an exceptional player. So…

of the other two horns was extremely perilous. Clark Terry was playing the trumpet and Wardell Grey (PHONETIC) was playing the tenor saxophone and if you couldn't play, you just as well go home with them.
